explanation: Exchanging business cards is a standard and important part of business etiquette in Singapore, much as in many other Asian countries. The way you treat a card is read as a sign of the respect you will show the person, so cards should be given and received with both hands (or the right hand only) and studied rather than pocketed.
local_tip: Present and receive cards with both hands with the writing facing the recipient, pause to read each card, and keep it on the table or in a cardholder rather than stuffing it into a pocket.

also_check.note: Card exchange (meishi) is a formal ritual with bows and careful reading of the card.
Two-handed exchange is expected, though casual pocketing is more tolerated than in Japan.
Cards are exchanged casually and one-handed; elaborate two-handed rituals can seem overly formal.
